washer.note: Kenmore has no official error-code reference on kenmore.com; sourced from Sears PartsDirect, operated by Sears Home Services, the same corporate family (Transformco) that owns Kenmore and the resource kenmore.com itself directs customers to. Direct page fetch was bot-blocked (403), so content was cross-verified via multiple independent search-snippet extractions.

codes.meaning: The machine isn't getting water into the tub, usually a shut supply valve or a pinched/iced fill line.
The sensor that reads water temperature is sending a bad signal, often a loose or damaged wiring connection.
The motor controller and the main control board have lost communication with each other mid-cycle.
The sensor that measures water pressure/level inside the tub is reporting an invalid reading.
The machine has detected more suds than it can handle, usually from non-HE detergent or too much of it.
On VMAX-style top-load models, the main control board's relay has failed in a stuck-on position.

oven.note: Sourced from Sears PartsDirect (Kenmore's corporate affiliate); direct fetch was bot-blocked, verified via search-snippet cross-check.

codes.meaning: A harmless status code appearing only when Cancel is held for several seconds with no real fault present.
The oven's main electronic control unit itself has failed.
The wiring between the keypad and the control board has come loose or disconnected.
The oven's temperature sensor circuit is reading incorrectly.
During a self-clean cycle, internal temperature exceeded roughly 950°F, treated as an overheat fault.

dryer.note: Sourced from Sears PartsDirect (Kenmore's corporate affiliate); direct fetch was bot-blocked, verified via search-snippet cross-check.

codes.meaning: Power to the dryer was interrupted mid-cycle; the cycle can simply be resumed once power is restored.
The dryer's main control board has failed internally.
A button on one of the console's touchpad assemblies is physically stuck down.
The relay on the main board that switches the heating element has failed.
The temperature sensor at the dryer's exhaust outlet has gone electrically open.
A second, related failure mode of the same exhaust-outlet temperature sensor.

dishwasher.note: Sourced from Sears PartsDirect (Kenmore's corporate affiliate); direct fetch was bot-blocked, verified via search-snippet cross-check.

codes.meaning: The dishwasher isn't getting enough water in, often a kinked, frozen, or shut-off supply line.
The unit isn't draining properly, usually a clogged or pinched drain hose.
An internal leak has been detected and the machine has stopped to prevent water damage.
The heating circuit has failed or incoming water is far hotter than the control expects.
The wash motor is malfunctioning.
The circulation (Vario) motor is malfunctioning.

refrigerator.note: Sourced from Sears PartsDirect (Kenmore's corporate affiliate); direct fetch was bot-blocked, verified via search-snippet cross-check.

codes.meaning: The freezer's temperature sensor or its wiring is faulty.
The small fan that circulates air through the ice compartment has stopped working.
The fan that cools the condenser coils has failed.
During defrost, the heater failed to warm the evaporator coil above about 46°F within the expected time.

freezer.note: Sourced from Sears PartsDirect (Kenmore's corporate affiliate); direct fetch was bot-blocked, verified via search-snippet cross-check.

codes.meaning: A button on the control panel is stuck, which a brief power cycle usually clears.
The internal temperature sensor (thermistor) has failed.
On deluxe electronic-control models, this flags the door being left open.
The control panel and the main electronic board have lost communication with each other.
The control panel's button lockout feature is active.
